description:
Found by the dual CI (defk-wfi.2), 2026-10-14, on native x86-64 (GitHub Actions linux-x86_64-clang) and under Rosetta; both agree.

Problem: test/report_test.exs 'report: :full dot's hot loop vectorises' and 'report: :full, a cache built in another directory gives the same facts as the directory that built it' assert a {:vectorize, :vectorized, _} fact for dot/2. On x86-64, clang 19 reports {:vectorize, :missed, "not vectorised: cannot prove it is safe to reorder floating-point operations ..."} for the same loop. The kernel is correct; the facts differ by target. The fast-path report is not part of the kernel subset (CONTEXT.md), so this is a test expectation, not a meaning change. It may still matter for performance claims: docs/performance.md numbers are arm64 only, and an x86-64 float reduction that does not vectorise could change rows of the Linux measurement run (defk-a1p).

Decide: make the assertions per target (vectorised on arm64, missed with the reorder reason on x86-64), or pick a kernel that vectorises on both for the cache test (it only needs some fact that survives the move). Note why arm64 clang vectorises an ordered f64 reduction and x86-64 does not, in docs/performance.md if it explains a measured difference.

Done when: both tests pass on linux-x86_64-clang and on arm64.

comments.text:
Resolution: fixed in the tests, merged to main.
- Decision: per-target assertions. dot's test now expects :vectorized with a width on arm64 and :missed with 'reorder floating-point' on x86-64. The moved-cache test needs only some {:vectorize, _, _} fact; its equality check already compares every fact.
- No docs change: docs/performance.md 6.17 already records it (arm64 vectorises in-order float reductions as ordered reductions; x86-64 at SSE2/v2/v3/v4 does not). For the Linux measurement run (defk-a1p): float reductions like sum, dot and cosine stay scalar on x86-64; partial sums vectorise on both.
- Results: report_test 17/17 on macOS, Linux x86-64 clang (Rosetta; the remarks are compile-time, so exact), Linux aarch64 clang. macOS mix ci 1736/1736.

title: Fast-path report tests expect arm64 vectorisation facts; x86-64 clang does not vectorise dot
